title: notes selects outputs without consuming release intent

setupFiles..changeset/ui-feature.md:
---
"@acme/ui": feature
---

Copy link button on the profile screen
setupFiles..changeset/api-fix.md:
---
"@acme/api": fix
---

Honor the caller's abort signal

expectation: `monochange notes` is read-only: `--output` selects a configured output, `--target` narrows it to one release owner, `--file` redirects the render to exactly the named path (stdout stays empty — it is a redirect, not a tee), and `--file -` is stdout. A user-stream output renders only user-stream changes and a default-stream target renders only its own, so neither note leaks the other audience. Unknown output ids fail with the valid names. Nothing is consumed: the changeset files are still on disk afterwards, which is what makes notes safe to run repeatedly while drafting.

checks.command: monochange notes --output user > .n.out 2>/dev/null; rc=$?; grep -q 'Copy link button' .n.out; a=$?; grep -q 'abort signal' .n.out; b=$?; rm -f .n.out; test $rc -eq 0 -a $a -eq 0 -a $b -eq 1
checks.why: The user stream must carry the customer-facing change and must not leak the developer detail; both halves matter, since a leak defeats the split as surely as an omission.

checks.command: monochange notes --output default --target @acme/api > .n.out 2>/dev/null; rc=$?; grep -q 'abort signal' .n.out; a=$?; grep -q 'Copy link button' .n.out; b=$?; rm -f .n.out; test $rc -eq 0 -a $a -eq 0 -a $b -eq 1
checks.why: The default output spans several owners, so without `--target` it refuses with an ambiguity error; with the target it must render that package's change only.

checks.command: monochange notes --output does-not-exist > .n.out 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -q 'user' .n.out; a=$?; rm -f .n.out; test $rc -eq 1 -a $a -eq 0
checks.why: A misspelled output id must fail loudly and name what does exist, which is how an agent recovers instead of assuming the note was rendered.

checks.command: monochange notes --output user --file notes.md > .stdout.out 2>/dev/null; rc=$?; test -f notes.md; a=$?; grep -q 'Copy link button' notes.md; b=$?; test ! -s .stdout.out; c=$?; rm -f notes.md .stdout.out; test $rc -eq 0 -a $a -eq 0 -a $b -eq 0 -a $c -eq 0
checks.why: `--file` is a redirect, not a tee: the note goes to the named path and stdout stays empty, so a CI consumer cannot double-print the artifact. Pinning the redirect keeps an agent from assuming it will also see the note on stdout.
Unlike `prepare`, notes is a read over release intent. Both changeset files must still be present after every check above ran, which is what makes the command safe to iterate on.

checks.command: monochange notes --output user --file - > .n.out 2>/dev/null; rc=$?; grep -q 'Copy link button' .n.out; a=$?; rm -f .n.out; test $rc -eq 0 -a $a -eq 0
checks.why: `--file -` is the explicit stdout form; pinning it stops an agent from inventing a redirection convention the CLI does not document.
